# denfluxR

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

`denfluxR` is the R interface for the [DenFlux Python engine](https://github.com/Mianzhi-Wang/DenFlux) (also available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/denflux/)). It provides a process-based computational framework to dynamically reconstruct the corrected zero-flow baseline for Granier thermal dissipation probes using machine learning (Random Forest) and physiological constraints.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `denfluxR` from [GitHub](https://github.com/Mianzhi-Wang/denfluxR) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("Mianzhi-Wang/denfluxR")
```

### Python Backend Setup

`denfluxR` relies on the `denflux` Python package. Once you have installed `denfluxR` in R, you must configure the backend engine by running:

``` r
library(denfluxR)
install_denflux()
```
*This will automatically create an isolated Conda/Virtual environment and install the required Python dependencies via `reticulate`.*

## Basic Usage

Here is a quick example of how to process your sap flow data:

``` r
library(denfluxR)

# Assuming you have a dataframe named 'my_data'
# result <- process(
#   data = my_data,
#   time_col = "Time",
#   dayfirst = TRUE,
#   Radiation = "PAR",
#   night_threshold = 10,
#   growstart = 5,
#   growend = 9
# )
# head(result)
```

For more detailed information and visualization examples, please refer to the package vignette.
